chunks: And from him, from Uthman, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the garment dyed with saffron: do I wash it and enter into ihram while wearing it? He said, 'There is no harm with it.'

key_terms.أُحْرِمُ: I enter into ihram (the sacred state for pilgrimage)
key_terms.الزَّعْفَرَانِ: Saffron, a yellow spice used as a dye
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm with it (it is permissible)

ai.seo_question: Do I need to wash my saffron-dyed clothes before entering ihram for Hajj?
ai.summary: Sa'id ibn Yasar asked Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) whether a pilgrim needs to wash a garment dyed with saffron before entering the state of ihram for Hajj or Umrah. The Imam ruled that there is no harm in entering ihram while wearing it without washing, indicating that saffron dye does not render the garment impure or invalid for ihram. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between mere scent or color and the specific prohibition of wool or silk, emphasizing that natural dyes like saffron do not invalidate the sanctity of the ihram state.
